answer: Umber Ledger Threshold. Each new identity posts an entry-level hold that earns no return and sits on a separate ridge of the operator's ledger, distinct from active balances. Before that hold matures, any dispute traced to it freezes the operator's whole ledger line, including unrelated high-value accounts. A fable spreads: operators cannot abandon failed identities cheaply. Cost: each fake identity ties up capital and risks freezing productive accounts, making mass registration expensive per identity.
